publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We describe latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model for collections of discrete data such as text corpora.

span.label: topic modelling of document collections
span.quote: In this paper we consider the problem of modeling text corpora and other collections of discrete data.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We present efficient approximate inference techniques based on variational methods and an EM algorithm for empirical Bayes parameter estimation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a generative probabilistic model: each document is a finite mixture over latent topics, and each topic a distribution over words
span.quote: each item of a collection is modeled as a finite mixture over an underlying set of topics

span.label: The bag-of-words (exchangeability) assumption can split words that belong to a single phrase across different topics.
span.note: what this limits: every topic assignment over multi-word names and phrases: THE BAG-OF-WORDS ASSUMPTION ALLOWS WORDS THAT SHOULD BE GENERATED BY THE SAME TOPIC (E.G., 'WILLIAM RANDOLPH HEARST FOUNDATION') TO BE ALLOCATED TO SEVERAL DIFFERENT TOPICS
span.quote: In particular, the bag-of-words assumption allows words that should be generated by the same topic (e.g., “William Randolph Hearst Foundation”) to be allocated to several different topics.

span.label: The text-classification results are presented as preliminary and needing further support.
span.note: what this limits: the text-classification result: ALTHOUGH THESE RESULTS NEED FURTHER SUBSTANTIATION, THEY SUGGEST THAT THE TOPIC-BASED REPRESENTATION ... MAY BE USEFUL AS A FAST FILTERING ALGORITHM
span.quote: Although these results need further substantiation, they suggest that the topic-based representation provided by LDA may be useful as a fast filtering algorithm for feature selection in text classification.

span.label: Exact posterior inference in LDA cannot be done; only approximate inference is available.
span.note: what this limits: any topic solution treated as the posterior: EXACT INFERENCE IS INTRACTABLE FOR LDA, and only approximate inference algorithms are available
span.quote: Exact inference is intractable for LDA, but any of a large suite of approximate inference algorithms can be used for inference and parameter estimation within the LDA framework.

span.label: The authors disclaim any epistemological claim about the variables they call topics.
span.note: what this limits: any interpretation of a fitted topic as a theme or subject: the authors state they use the word topics to exploit text-oriented intuitions and make no epistemological claims about these latent variables beyond their utility in representing probability distributions on sets of words
span.quote: We refer to the latent multinomial variables in the LDA model as topics, so as to exploit text-oriented intuitions, but we make no epistemological claims regarding these latent variables beyond their utility in representing probability distributions on sets of words

span.label: The text vocabulary is stated to be an aid to intuition, and the model is not tied to text.
span.note: what this limits: any humanities reading of this model's output: the authors state the language of text collections is used to guide intuition and that the LDA model is not necessarily tied to text
span.quote: We use the language of text collections throughout the paper, referring to entities such as “words,” “documents,” and “corpora.” This is useful in that it helps to guide intuition, particularly when we introduce latent variables which aim to capture abstract notions such as topics. It is important to note, however, that the LDA model is not necessarily tied to text

span.label: Documents as well as words are assumed exchangeable, which the authors note is less often stated.
span.note: what this limits: any use of a topic model over a corpus with an order that matters, such as a diachronic study: the methods assume documents are exchangeable, so the specific ordering of documents in a corpus can be neglected, which the authors note is less often stated formally
span.quote: All of these methods are based on the “bag-of-words” assumption—that the order of words in a document can be neglected. In the language of probability theory, this is an assumption of exchangeability for the words in a document (Aldous, 1985). Moreover, although less often stated formally, these methods also assume that documents are exchangeable; the specific ordering of the documents in a corpus can also be neglected

span.label: perplexity
span.quote: The perplexity, used by convention in language modeling, is monotonically decreasing in the likelihood of the test data, and is algebraicly equivalent to the inverse of the geometric mean per-word likelihood

span.label: a topic - A LATENT MULTINOMIAL VARIABLE, NAMED TO BORROW A MEANING IT DOES NOT CLAIM: the authors say they call these variables topics in order to exploit text-oriented intuitions, and in the same sentence make no epistemological claims about them beyond representing probability distributions over words; the word appears about a hundred times in the body and the disclaimer once, in a footnote

It is important to note, however, that the LDA model is not necessarily tied to text

span.label: exchangeability - TWO ASSUMPTIONS, ONE OF THEM USUALLY LEFT UNSAID: words within a document are exchangeable, which is the bag-of-words assumption everyone states, and DOCUMENTS are exchangeable too, which the authors say is less often stated formally - the second is what removes time from a corpus

In the language of probability theory, this is an assumption of exchangeability for the words in a document (Aldous, 1985). Moreover, although less often stated formally, these methods also assume that documents are exchangeable; the specific ordering of the documents in a corpus can also be neglected

span.label: builds-on → hierarchical Bayesian modeling
span.quote: LDA is a three-level hierarchical Bayesian model

span.label: contradicts → LSI (latent semantic indexing) methodology
span.quote: it is not clear why one should adopt the LSI methodology

span.label: extends → Hofmann (1999) probabilistic latent semantic indexing (pLSI) model
span.quote: LDA overcomes both of these problems by treating the topic mixture weights as a k-parameter hidden random variable rather than a large set of individual parameters which are explicitly linked to the training set.

span.label: contradicts → Hofmann's pLSI treatment of documents
span.note: differs in: THE PARAMETER IS THE LEVEL AT WHICH THE MODEL IS PROBABILISTIC. The span: 'While Hofmann's work is a useful step toward probabilistic modeling of text, IT IS INCOMPLETE IN THAT IT PROVIDES NO PROBABILISTIC MODEL AT THE LEVEL OF DOCUMENTS.' The contradiction is not global - pLSI is granted as a useful step - and it turns on one named thing. Q-437.
span.quote: While Hofmann’s work is a useful step toward probabilistic modeling of text, it is incomplete in that it provides no probabilistic model at the level of documents.

span.label: builds-on → de Finetti (1990) representation theorem for exchangeable random variables
span.quote: A classic representation theorem due to de Finetti (1990) establishes that any collection of exchangeable random variables has a representation as a mixture distribution—in general an infinite mixture.

span.label: builds-on → Nigam et al. (2000) mixture of unigrams model
span.quote: If we augment the unigram model with a discrete random topic variable z (Figure 3b), we obtain a mixture of unigrams model (Nigam et al., 2000).

span.label: LDA is a generative probabilistic (three-level hierarchical Bayesian) model for text corpora: each document is a finite mixture over latent topics, each topic a distribution over words — giving an explicit topic-based representation of documents.
span.quote: latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model for collections of discrete data such as text corpora. LDA is a three-level hierarchical Bayesian model, in which each item of a collection is modeled as a finite mixture over an underlying set of topics.

span.label: Efficient approximate inference via variational methods + EM; LDA outperforms mixture-of-unigrams and probabilistic LSI on document modeling, text classification, and collaborative filtering.
span.quote: We present efficient approximate inference techniques based on variational methods and an EM algorithm for empirical Bayes parameter estimation. We report results in document modeling, text classification, and collaborative filtering, comparing to a mixture of unigrams model and the probabilistic LSI model.

span.label: observed word counts per document (bag-of-words)
span.quote: for each document in the corpus, a count is formed of the number of occurrences of each word

span.label: latent topic mixture / topic-word distributions
span.quote: each item of a collection is modeled as a finite mixture over an underlying set of topics

span.label: latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA)
span.quote: latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model for collections of discrete data such as text corpora

span.label: topic (as word distribution)
span.quote: Each topic is, in turn, modeled as an infinite mixture over an underlying set of topic probabilities

span.label: tf-idf scheme
span.quote: In the popular tf-idf scheme (Salton and McGill, 1983), a basic vocabulary of “words” or “terms” is chosen, and, for each document in the corpus, a count is formed

span.label: Bayesian
span.quote: LDA is a three-level hierarchical Bayesian model, in which each item of a collection is modeled as a finite mixture over an underlying set of topics.

span.label: mean
span.quote: Laplace smoothing is commonly used; this essentially yields the mean of the posterior distribution under a uniform Dirichlet prior on the multinomial parameters.
